content:
Students at Escuela Secundaria General No. 7 Gral. Emiliano Zapata in Nuevo Laredo marked two traditions in one school celebration, combining Pumpkin Day with Día de Muertos, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The assembly, coordinated by arts and music teacher Emmanuel Castillo González, brought the school community together with parents as special guests. The catrina and catrín runway took place on the school esplanade.

For Pumpkin Day, students carved and decorated pumpkins as fantasy, cartoon, and movie characters as part of their English classes. The pumpkins were exhibited during the school's cultural and artistic day, building on classroom lessons about the origin of Pumpkin Day and Halloween traditions in the neighboring United States.

The Día de Muertos portion included an introduction to the history of the holiday and the meaning of the altar, a theater performance, and students reading literary calaveritas. About 25 students took part in the catrina and catrín runway, judged on bearing, costume, makeup, and partner dancing to select first-place winners. The article did not name the winners.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Nuevo Laredo: Celebran 'Pumpkin Day' y Día de Muertos en la Secundaria 7," November 1, 2026
